Expert 1 here — the classifier that reads the structured panel and nothing else. My bid:

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.88
  uncertainty  +/- 0.05 epistemic (95% band 0.78-0.98); among patients I cannot tell apart the outcome was 0.52 of 1.00 mixed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 88% of the time over the 33 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most, across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, PI-RADS >= 4, no prior biopsy, pmhx_hypercholesterolaemia, suspicious DRE, number of comorbidities. I read 39 variables, all
from the panel — nothing from the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the previous notes or the
laboratory. Out-of-fold over 91 labelled cases: AUC 0.758, balanced
accuracy 0.625.

The final call is the chair's.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The guideline suggests that a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger a biopsy. It also notes that MRI-directed US-guided prostate biopsy is now the standard of care.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED, I disagree with the high probability of biopsy because the guideline emphasizes that the decision must be risk-adapted, and the panel variables alone do not settle the indication. EXPERT-COHORT, your criterion is insufficient because the guideline requires a specific finding from an opened document to confirm the decision, not just the panel numbers.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the prior biopsy status: None means the indication stands based on the guideline's general approach for PI-RADS 5.
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: Unchanged does not support re-sampling, new or larger does
psa_trend - the PSA velocity: The guideline does not provide a specific threshold for PSA velocity in this context.
laboratory_results - the PSA density: The guideline suggests a PSA-D cut-off of 0.15 ng/mL/cc may guide the decision.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: INDETERMINATE (uncertain). Last value 6.77 ng/mL over 4 points spanning 13 months; velocity +4.27 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 5 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 8.2 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 2.3-28.4.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.85
  uncertainty  +/- 0.06 epistemic (95% band 0.73-0.96), of which 0.00 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

data.gist: Expert 3 suggests BIOPSY, p=0.85 +/- 0.06, HIGH reliability (firm, fusion_nolab)

interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents retrieved by the registrar appear to have answered all three moderator questions. The `radiology_report` addressed Q1 by stating "COMPARISON: 'new'". The `psa_trend` addressed Q2 by indicating a "significant upward trajectory." The `previous_notes` addressed Q3 by stating "Prior biopsy: None. Surveillance protocol: A subsequent blood draw has been planned for later in the year to monitor trends."

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence supports the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY. Specifically, the PI-RADS 5 finding from the `radiology_report` and the PSA velocity from the `psa_trend` align with the cohort criterion that fired the panel decision.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What does the radiology_report state regarding whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study? Answered by the `radiology_report`: "COMPARISON: 'new'".
Q2. What does the psa_trend indicate regarding the PSA velocity? Answered by the `psa_trend`: "The PSA velocity shows a rise from 0.5 (Jan 2024) to 6.77 (Feb 2025), indicating a significant upward trajectory."
Q3. What does the previous_notes state regarding the prior biopsy status, surveillance protocol, and planned treatment? Answered by the `previous_notes`: "Prior biopsy: None. Surveillance protocol: A subsequent blood draw has been planned for later in the year to monitor trends."

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 5 finding from the `radiology_report` is the most decisive variable as it directly relates to the cohort criterion that drove the panel decision. The PSA velocity from the `psa_trend` is also highly relevant as it indicates a significant upward trajectory, which supports the need for action.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a biopsy, as the retrieved evidence strongly aligns with the panel's decision based on the PI-RADS 5 finding and the significant PSA velocity.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
